# model_schema_tool

> Discover schema, columns, required fields, and available FILTERS for a model.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `data` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations (default); grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=model_schema_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Discover schema, columns, required fields, and available FILTERS for a model.

ALWAYS use this tool BEFORE general_crud_tool to:
- Get available filters for the model (returned in special_filters)
- Understand required fields for create operations
- See column types and associations

RETURNS: columns, api_fields, required_fields, associations, special_filters, search_term_examples, notes

EXAMPLE: {model_name: "Individual"} returns filters like role_type_id, first_name, last_name, email, phone

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_name` | string | yes | Name of the model to inspect (e.g., Contact, Party, Individual) |

## Example

```json
{"name": "model_schema_tool", "arguments": {"model_name": "Task"}}
```

Returns `columns`, `api_fields`, `required_fields`, `associations`, `special_filters`
(the names you can pass in `general_crud_tool`'s `filters`), `search_term_examples` and `notes`.

## Gotchas

- **Call this before your first `general_crud_tool` list or create on a model.** Filter names
  are model-specific and not guessable.

## Input schema

The JSON Schema served for `inputSchema`, verbatim.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "model_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Name of the model to inspect (e.g., Contact, Party, Individual)"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "model_name"
  ]
}
```
